nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original form is المتدثر; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl because they are from the same point of articulation. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: he was covered with a velvet cloth (قطيفة). ʿIkrima said: i.e. "I have covered you (دثّرت) with this matter, so carry it out."

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: Qatāda said: i.e. warn of Allah's punishment and His blows against the nations. Abū Jaʿfar said: so the construction according to Qatāda's view is: "warn them of these things", and then this was omitted because it is indicated [by the context].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: I.e. magnify Him by worshipping Him alone; and it [رَبَّكَ] is accusative by كبّر.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t: وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ (4): [ثِيابَكَ is] accusative by طهّر. وَالرُّجْزَ is accusative by فاهجر. Even if the verbs had the hāʾ [i.e. an object pronoun], the accusative would still be preferable, because the command is better construed with a verb.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَلا تَمْنُنْ is jussive (majzūm) because of the prohibition, and the doubling was made overt because the second [nūn] is vowelless. If it were in [ordinary] speech, لا تمنّ would be permissible, with fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma on the nūn. Khaṣīf «[Translator's note: the source has «حصيف»; the narrator from Mujāhid is usually Khuṣayf.]» related from Mujāhid, who said: لا تَمْنُنْ means "do not weaken". Abū Jaʿfar said: it would be taken from المنين, which means "weak", and the construction would be: "and do not weaken from seeking much good" — then «أن» was dropped and the verb put in the nominative. Ibn Zayd said: [it means] do not count it as a favour to people that you convey the message, in order to gain much from them. Abū Jaʿfar said: the most appropriate thing said about the meaning — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best — is: do not count as a favour your obedience and your conveying of the message, deeming it much; and this is the meaning of al-Ḥasan's view. Abū Jaʿfar said: we said this is more appropriate because it fits the context of the speech better, since the passage contains a warning and a command to patience and to diligence in obedience.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: The deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil; lit. "the noun of that whose agent is not named"), according to Sībawayh, is فِي النَّاقُورِ; and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās it is a latent (mustatir) pronoun indicated by the verb.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: فَذلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); يَوْمَئِذٍ may be a badal (substitute) from it, and it has fatḥa because it is indeclinable (mabnī), just as مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ [al-Maʿārij: 11] has been read [with fatḥa]; and it may be accusative in the sense "I mean". يَوْمٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the subject; عَسِيرٌ is its naʿt (adjective), and likewise غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: مَنْ is in the position of naṣb (accusative), either as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the nūn and the yāʾ [of ذَرْنِي]. وَحِيداً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: لَهُ is in the position of the second object.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Since it [the bāʾ of بَنِينَ] has a vowel, the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) was dropped; and on this basis they said in the relative adjective (nisba): بنويّ. Sībawayh permitted «ابنيّ», and some of the Kufans disallowed it.

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: كَلَّا is a rejection of his greed and a deterrent to him. إِنَّهُ كانَ لِآياتِنا عَنِيداً: in the sense of معاند (obstinately opposing).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً (17): ʿAṭiyya related from Abū Saʿīd from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "He will be made to climb a steep slope; when he puts his hand on it, it melts, and when he puts his foot on it, it melts."

nahhas-irab:18-19.t: إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ (18), i.e. he thought about refuting the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and he went back time after time, considering whether he could refute them; and he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, without disagreement. Qatāda said: they claim that he thought about what the Prophet brought and said: "By Allah, it is not poetry; it has a sweetness and a grace upon it, and in my view it is nothing but magic." So Allah the Exalted revealed: فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ (19). Abū Jaʿfar said: the view of al-Farrāʾ is that قتل means "he was cursed". Abū Jaʿfar said: according to the speech of the Arabs, قتل must mean "he was destroyed", because one who is killed is destroyed.

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: I.e. he contracted [the skin] between his eyes and frowned, when it became hard for him to refute the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ from the truth وَاسْتَكْبَرَ: so Allah reported of his ignorance that he was too proud to believe in the signs of Allah and His Messenger — after a refutation of what he brought was [not] possible for him «[Translator's note: so in the source («بعد أن يتهيأ له ردّ ما جاء به»); the sense seems to require "after a refutation was not possible for him".]» — yet he was not too proud to prostrate to stones that neither benefit nor harm.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t: فَقالَ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ (24): when he found no argument, he disbelieved; then he said: إِنْ هذا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ (25). So he added to his ignorance something that is not hidden, because the Prophet ﷺ had challenged them — and they were Arabs like him — to produce a sūra like it, and they were unable to do so; and if it were the speech of a human being, what was possible for him would have been possible for them.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: It has been said: [سَقَرَ] is a diptote because it is the name of a feminine; and it has been said: because it is a foreign noun. The first is correct, because a foreign noun of three letters is declinable [as a triptote], even if its middle letter is vowelled; and moreover it is an Arabic noun with a derivation: one says سقرته الشمس, when the sun burns him; and السّاقور is a piece of iron that is heated and used to brand the donkey.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: The clause is in the position of naṣb (accusative) by إدراك [i.e. أَدْراكَ], except that what precedes an interrogative does not operate on it «[Translator's note: the source has «لا يعلم فيه», apparently a misprint of «لا يعمل فيه», "does not govern it"; translated accordingly.]».

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: It may be asked: why was the wāw dropped from «تذر», when it is only dropped in «يذر»? «[Translator's note: so in the source; the question is apparently why the wāw is dropped in يذر at all.]» And if it is said: its pattern is يفعل, it will be asked: [then why] the fatḥa, when it contains no guttural letter? The answer was given by Ibn Kaysān: since يذر has the same meaning as يدع, in that no past tense of it is pronounced and the meaning of the two is one, they made it follow it [in form].

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: [لَوَّاحَةٌ is nominative] on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is لوّاحة to البشر", i.e. to the creatures; and it [البشر] may be the plural of بشرة ("skin").

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ is] in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), except that it has fatḥa because the conjunction wāw was dropped from it, so it was given its vowel. And it has been said: it was heavy, so it was given the lightest of the vowels, because they are two nouns originally. The grammarians differed on forming the relative adjective (nisba) from the two. The view of Sībawayh and a group of grammarians is that when you form the nisba from the two, you drop the second and form the nisba from the first, so you say تسعيّ; أحدي for أحد عشر, and بعلي in the nisba of بعلبكّ. The other view is that the nisba is formed from both of them together and nothing else, so that one says تسعة عشريّ and بعلبكيّ. Abū al-ʿAbbās Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā rejected the first view and said: they are two nouns that express one meaning, so if you drop the second its meaning is lost; so only the nisba from both together is permissible. He argued from what the grammarians agree on in their saying هذا حبّ رمانيّ and جحر ضبيّ — he attached [the nisba] to the second and did not drop it — and likewise هذا أبو عمريّ. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: this is stronger in the nisba — meaning: هذا تسعة عشريّ, معدي كربيّ and بعلبكيّ. Al-Farrāʾ permitted جاءني أحد عشر with a sukūn on the ʿayn, and likewise from ثلاثة عشر to تسعة عشر; but he does not permit this in اثني عشر, so as not to combine two vowelless letters, nor does he permit it in the feminine, so as not to combine two vowelless letters. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said is not far-fetched; it has been related from Abū Jaʿfar that he read عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowels; the reading meant is apparently تِسْعَةَ عْشَرَ, with a sukūn on the ʿayn.]».

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: أَصْحابَ is the plural of صاحب, with the additional letter dropped, because أفعال is not the plural of فاعل without dropping; and أفعال is the plural of eight patterns, among which are neither فاعل nor فعل «[Translator's note: so in the source; the second pattern may be a different vowelling of فعل that has been lost in print.]». وَما جَعَلْنا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, i.e. a hardship and a test of devotion, so that they disbelieve; so that they know that Allah is able to strengthen and support these angels. لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ: the lām of kay (purpose), and its origin is that it is the lām of the genitive, because the meaning is: "for the certainty of those who were given the Book". وَيَزْدادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيماناً is conjoined to the first, and likewise وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ. Then the lām was repeated, and if it had not been brought it would have been permissible, in وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْكافِرُونَ ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا. «ما» is in the position of naṣb (accusative) by أراد, and it and ذا are treated as one thing; but if you make «ذا» mean "which" (الذي), then ما is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), ذا is its khabar (predicate), and what comes after it is its ṣila (relative clause). كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ: the kāf is in the position of naṣb as a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar. وَما يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ: [هُوَ is] nominative by يعلم, and the accusative as an exception is not permissible; and likewise وَما هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ. Mujāhid said: i.e. the Fire is nothing but a reminder to mankind. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr mentioned that the full stop is at كَلَّا, on the understanding that the meaning is: the matter is not as the polytheist said to his fellow polytheists, "I will deal with the keepers of the Fire for you". وَالْقَمَرِ is an oath, i.e. "by the Lord of the moon".

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: ] «[Translator's note: the source begins with a stray bracket, and the first reading being described has dropped out of the text; it is presumably وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا دَبَرَ.]» is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ḥamza and Nāfiʿ read وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: the correct view is that دبر and أدبر have the same meaning; this is what the exegetes and most of the lexicographers say. «إذا» is for the future and «إذ» for the past. As for the statement of Abū ʿUbayd that he chooses «إذا دبر» because after it comes وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا أَسْفَرَ — [this is not binding,] because Allah the Exalted swears by whatever He wills, and no judgement may be imposed on that requiring both to be future or both past.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: «[Translator's note: the source begins with «أن إن», apparently a corruption.]» "The Fire is one of the enormous matters." Abū Razīn said: «إنها», i.e. Jahannam. And الْكُبَرِ [is] with alif and lām; dropping them is not permissible according to any grammarian, and nothing of this [pattern] has come in the speech of the Arabs without alif and lām except أخر, and for that reason it was made a diptote.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
Al-Ḥasan said: there is no warner more calamitous than the Fire — or words to that effect. Abū Razīn said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am a warner to mankind". Ibn Zayd said: Muḥammad ﷺ is a warner to mankind. Abū Jaʿfar said: these are the views of the exegetes, and the closest [interpretations] can be derived from them. On the accusative of نذير there are seven views. It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أنا» «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the pronoun in «إنها» is meant.]»; and it may be a ḥāl from إحدى الكبر. These two views are derived from the view of al-Ḥasan, because he made the Fire the one that warns. The construction may be: "and none knows the hosts of your Lord except He, as a warner to mankind"; and the construction may be: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it thus, a warner to mankind" — these two views are derived from the view of Abū Razīn. Al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. "Stand, as a warner" — and this goes back to the view of Ibn Zayd. And نذير may mean "warning" (إنذار), as He said:
«فكيف كان نذير»; the construction would then be: "and We have made the keepers of the Fire nothing but angels, as a warning". Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the construction may be "I mean, a warner". Abū Jaʿfar said: the tāʾ «[Translator's note: the source has «الياء» (yāʾ); the feminine tāʾ is evidently meant.]» was dropped from نذير, when it refers to the Fire, in the sense of attribution (nasab).

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: [لِمَنْ شاءَ is] a badal (substitute) with the lām repeated; and without the lām it would have been permissible.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: رَهِينَةٌ is construed according to the meaning; if it were according to the wording, it would be رهين.

nahhas-irab:39-41.t: [أَصْحابَ is] accusative as an exception. It is soundly reported from two of the Companions of the Prophet that by أصحاب اليمين here are meant the angels and the children. What indicates this is that after it comes يَتَساءَلُونَ عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ ما سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ, and this is the speech of those who have committed no sin. Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reading: يَتَساءَلُونَ عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يا فلان ما سلكك في سقر. This reading is by way of explanation (tafsīr), and its chain of transmission is sound.

nahhas-irab:42-44.t:
وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ: the nūn was dropped because of frequent use; if it were brought, it would be good outside the Qur'an. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the nūn resembled the nūn that is dropped in the jussive in our saying:
يقومان and يقومون. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab said: he is mistaken; if it were as he said, it would be dropped in our saying لم يصن زيد نفسه.

nahhas-irab:45-47.t: وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الْخائِضِينَ: the kāf was given ḍamma to indicate that it is from a root with wāw, so فعل was transferred to فعل «[Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the two patterns (fa‘ala → fa‘ula) has been lost in print.]». And likewise وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ حَتَّى أَتانَا الْيَقِينُ, i.e. "until"; and «أن» is implied after «حتى».

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: I.e. the intercessors do not intercede for them; and by this He indicated that intercession benefits others than them.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «[Translator's note: the beginning of the entry, naming the first reading (مُسْتَنْفَرَةٌ, with fatḥa on the fāʾ), has dropped out of the source.]» [This is] the reading of the people of Medina and al-Ḥasan; and the reading of Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and Abū ʿAmr is مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ; and both readings are reported from al-Kisāʾī. Abū Jaʿfar said: «مستنفرة» [with kasra] is clearer in this, i.e. frightened; and مستنفرة [with fatḥa] is problematic «[Translator's note: the source text does not mark which vowel is meant in either case; the bracketed vowels follow the sense of the argument.]», because استفعل is mostly used when one seeks the action, as you say استسقى, when he asks to be given drink; and donkeys do not seek this. But the justification of the reading is that استنفر is in the sense of نفر, so the meaning is "fleeing".

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: [قَسْوَرَةٍ is] فعولة «[Translator's note: so in the source.]» from القسر. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned what the exegetes said about it.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: أَنْ يُؤْتى صُحُفاً مُنَشَّرَةً: [مُنَشَّرَةً is] according to the feminine of the group; and it was put in the singular because it is greater in number.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: Only assimilation (idghām) is permissible, because the first is vowelless.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: «وما تذكرون» is the reading of Nāfiʿ, with a shift of address; and most people read وَما يَذْكُرُونَ, so that it refers back to what preceded. وما تشاؤون إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ: with the object omitted because the hearer knows it. هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوى: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ: «أهل» was repeated for emphasis and magnification; and if it had not been repeated, it would have been permissible.
